stem: Meena's father is setting up a shaving mirror at home that must give an enlarged image of the face, and her school is making a solar cooker that must concentrate sunlight at one point. Which optical element should be used for both purposes?

options.text: a plane mirror, because it always shows things clearly
a convex mirror, because it gives a wide view
a concave mirror, because it can form an enlarged image and also converge light to a focus
a convex lens, because it can form an enlarged image but cannot be used in a solar cooker

teacher.key_rationale: A concave mirror gives an enlarged erect image when the face is inside its focal length (shaving/dental use) and converges parallel sunlight to its focus (solar cooker). Plane mirrors neither enlarge nor concentrate; convex mirrors diverge light and give diminished images; a convex lens concentrates light but is not used as a shaving mirror. Key C.
